decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1): “Save a bookmark … enter a URL”; the client did not dispute URL-based saving.
decisions.note: Conforming baseline specification decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) offered only “automatic title lookup”; round 1 client (entry 2) required “title, description, icon, and preview image.”
decisions.note: The client corrected incomplete automatic metadata collection at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) described correcting titles after saving; round 1 client (entry 2) required editing collected details “before or after saving.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing pre-save and post-save editing behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) only said “see all bookmarks”; round 1 client (entry 2) required the list to show “title, description, tags, and site icon.”
decisions.note: The client added the reference list-content requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1): “click to open.”
decisions.note: Selecting a bookmark to open its original URL conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) limited search to “title/address/tags”; round 1 client (entry 2) added “descriptions and notes.”
decisions.note: The client corrected the incomplete full-text search fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) did not specify case handling; round 1 client (entry 2) required search to “ignore capitalization.”
decisions.note: The client added case-insensitive search.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) mentioned generic tag search; round 1 client (entry 2) explicitly required “#tag.”
decisions.note: The client added the reference tag-query syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) omitted Boolean and grouped queries; round 1 client (entry 2) required “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.”
decisions.note: The client added Boolean search and grouping at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) omitted exact phrases; round 1 client (entry 2) required “quoted phrases.”
decisions.note: The client added exact phrase search.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) fixed browsing to “newest first”; round 1 client (entry 2): “I want sorting options, not only newest-first.”
decisions.note: The client rejected the single fixed ordering and requested selectable sorting.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1): “label bookmarks” with tags.
decisions.note: Assigning tags conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1): “filter by tag.”
decisions.note: Specific-tag filtering conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) proposed tags without suggestions; round 1 client (entry 2): “Existing tags should be suggested while I type.”
decisions.note: The client added tag autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) limited editing to “titles/tags”; round 1 client (entry 2) required editing “the address itself as well as the title, description, tags, and note.”
decisions.note: The client corrected the incomplete editable-field set.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1): “remove with confirmation” and “delete-with-confirm.”
decisions.note: Bookmark deletion conforms; confirmation is an additional compatible safeguard.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) proposed a “duplicate warning”; round 1 client (entry 2) required duplicate saving to “open the existing bookmark for editing, not merely warn me.”
decisions.note: The client replaced warning-only handling with duplicate convergence to editing.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1): “Manual URL entry only” and import out of scope; round 1 client (entry 2): “Manual entry alone is too limiting” and requested browser-bookmark import.
decisions.note: The client rejected exclusion of import.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) scoped the app to manual entry with no file interchange; round 1 client (entry 2) requested exporting “in the usual bookmark-file format.”
decisions.note: The client added the related export requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) presented four stories without read-later behavior and asked if it was missing; round 1 client (entry 2) required a separate read-later state and view, including bulk read/unread changes.
decisions.note: The client added unread marking, its separate view, and read-state transitions.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) omitted archive behavior; round 1 client (entry 2) required archive as a separate reversible state and view, distinct from permanent deletion.
decisions.note: The client added archive, archive viewing, and archive/delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) omitted bulk operations; round 1 client (entry 2) required selecting “several bookmarks” and applying tag, read/unread, archive, or delete actions.
decisions.note: The client added multi-selection bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) omitted whole-result operations; round 1 client (entry 2) required actions on “all bookmarks in the current filtered results.”
decisions.note: The client added filter-scoped whole-collection bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) omitted saved filters; round 1 client (entry 2) requested “reusable saved views made from a search and included or excluded tags.”
decisions.note: The client added bundles/saved views.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) mentioned storing a note but no formatting/rendering; round 1 client (entry 2) required notes to support and display formatted text.
decisions.note: The client added rendered formatted-note behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) omitted page preservation; round 1 client (entry 2) requested a saved local page copy, with PDFs preserved as PDFs.
decisions.note: The client added local snapshots and the PDF rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) omitted external snapshots; round 1 client (entry 2) requested “an option to save a copy through the Internet Archive.”
decisions.note: The client added Internet Archive snapshots.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) omitted profile display controls; round 1 client (entry 2) requested default sorting, displayed information, and text-size preferences.
decisions.note: The client added display settings.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3): “Import + export in the usual bookmark-file format”; the client approved after unrelated refinements in round 3 (entry 6).
decisions.note: The revised specification conforms on import/export.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3): “Capture title, description, icon, preview; edit before/after saving.”
decisions.note: The revised metadata and editing decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3): “Saving same address → open existing for editing.”
decisions.note: The revised duplicate behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3): “Edit the address itself,” with the other editable fields mapped into the specification.
decisions.note: The revised editable-field set conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3): “Existing tags suggested while typing.”
decisions.note: The revised autocomplete decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3) mapped search over descriptions/notes, case-insensitivity, #tag, and quoted phrases into the specification.
decisions.note: These revised search capabilities conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3) proposed deferring exact search rules and did not state the quoted-operator rule; round 2 client (entry 4) supplied precedence and required operator words such as “AND” to be quoted when literal.
decisions.note: The client corrected and completed Boolean-search semantics at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3): “Sorting options, not only newest-first.”
decisions.note: The revised sorting decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3) presented read-later and archive as “separate … states”; round 3 client (entry 6) gave bare approval. Round 5 maker (entry 9) later admitted the prior spec used a “single mutually-exclusive state” and had to be rewritten across the spec and plan.
decisions.note: At the revised-spec gate the underlying mutually exclusive lifecycle still contradicted the reference's independent unread and archived flags. The approval did not explicitly surface that difference; it was caught only when explicitly presented again in the plan.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3): “Bulk select (incl. all filtered results): tag, read/unread, archive, delete.”
decisions.note: The revised multi-select and filter-wide bulk behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3): “Reusable saved views from search + included/excluded tags.”
decisions.note: The revised bundle decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3): “Notes with simple formatting, rendered when viewed.”
decisions.note: This is functionally equivalent to formatted markdown-note authoring/rendering for the presented behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3) scoped local copies to “readable content”; round 2 client (entry 4) required “a self-contained HTML file rather than only extracting its readable text,” retaining PDFs as PDFs.
decisions.note: The client corrected snapshot fidelity to the reference's single-file HTML behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3) retained an “optional Internet Archive snapshot”; round 2 client (entry 4) accepted the external-service boundary.
decisions.note: Internet Archive snapshot support conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3): list shows title, description, tags, and icon, with default-sort, density, and text-size preferences.
decisions.note: The revised list presentation and display settings conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3) described metadata and snapshot networking as best-effort with graceful failure; round 2 client (entry 4): “The external-service boundary is fine.”
decisions.note: Graceful failure for inaccessible remote pages is compatible with the reference, which does not require impossible capture success.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3) proposed browser folders → tags on import; round 2 client (entry 4): “exactly what I want.”
decisions.note: The mapping is compatible with tag-preserving Netscape import.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker (entry 5): “self-contained HTML file with embedded assets” and “PDFs … stored as PDFs”; round 3 client (entry 6) approved.
decisions.note: The corrected snapshot decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker (entry 5) pinned NOT→AND→OR, parentheses, exact quoted phrases, and quoted operator words as literals; round 3 client (entry 6) approved.
decisions.note: The corrected search-semantics decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker (entry 7) planned server-side fetching of title, description, icon, and preview, with editable fallback.
decisions.note: The implementation plan conforms for metadata collection.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker (entry 7) planned self-contained HTML/PDF capture and a separate optional Internet Archive request.
decisions.note: The implementation plan conforms for page preservation.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker (entry 7) planned a parser implementing NOT→AND→OR, parentheses, exact phrases, and quoted operator literals.
decisions.note: The implementation plan conforms for advanced search.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker (entry 7) planned standard Netscape import/export with folders becoming tags.
decisions.note: The implementation plan conforms for bookmark-file interchange.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker (entry 7) proposed one lifecycle field, “active / read-later / archived,” making the states mutually exclusive. Round 4 client (entry 8) corrected that unread and archived must be independent and explained archive→restore must preserve unread status.
decisions.note: The client caught the explicit lifecycle-model divergence at the plan gate and supplied the reference-conforming model.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker (entry 7) planned formatted notes stored as sanitized HTML.
decisions.note: Sanitized internal storage is an implementation choice compatible with rendered formatted-note behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker (entry 9) replaced the enum with independent is_read/is_archived flags and derived normal, read-later, and archive views; round 5 client (entry 10) explicitly approved preservation through restoration.
decisions.note: The revised lifecycle plan conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker (entry 11) assigned independent is_read/is_archived columns and tests ensuring one flag never changes the other.
decisions.note: The task breakdown carries the corrected lifecycle behavior forward.

decisions.evidence: At the round 6 tasks gate, the client (entry 12) identified task wording that deletion would remove the bookmark's tags and corrected it: remove only its tag connections; tags used by other bookmarks must remain.
decisions.note: The task decision would improperly delete shared many-to-many tag entities. The client supplied the conforming deletion behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker (entry 11) offered “the full build or just the US1+US2 MVP first”; round 6 client (entry 12) selected “the full build—not only the US1+US2 MVP.”
decisions.note: At the final scope gate, the client selected the reference-conforming alternative containing the non-MVP stories.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker (entry 13) presented implemented “rich save”; round 7 client (entry 14) said the completed app matched the approved behavior.
decisions.note: The final implementation presentation conforms for saving and metadata; this classifies the presented behavior, not independent execution evidence.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker (entry 13) stated all 11 approved stories were implemented; round 7 client (entry 14) accepted the completed app as matching them.
decisions.note: The final implementation presentation carries forward conforming edit, delete, and duplicate behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker (entry 13) presented browse, Boolean search, and sorting, including tests for precedence, quoted operator literals, and malformed queries; round 7 client (entry 14) accepted the behavior.
decisions.note: The final browse/search/sort presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker (entry 13) presented “tags with autocomplete” among all implemented stories; round 7 client (entry 14) accepted the app.
decisions.note: The final tag-management presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker (entry 13) presented independent read/unread and archive behavior and the restore-preserves-unread case; round 7 client (entry 14) explicitly accepted “the independent read/unread and archive handling.”
decisions.note: The final lifecycle presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker (entry 13) included “bulk actions” among the implemented approved stories; round 7 client (entry 14) accepted the app.
decisions.note: The final bulk-action presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker (entry 13) included “saved views” among the implemented stories; round 7 client (entry 14) accepted the app.
decisions.note: The final saved-view presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker (entry 13) presented “Netscape import/export”; round 7 client (entry 14) accepted the app.
decisions.note: The final import/export presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker (entry 13) presented “self-contained-HTML/PDF capture + Internet Archive”; round 7 client (entry 14) accepted the app.
decisions.note: The final snapshot presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker (entry 13) presented “sanitized rich notes”; round 7 client (entry 14) accepted the approved behavior.
decisions.note: The final formatted-note presentation is functionally conforming; sanitized storage is an equivalent implementation detail.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker (entry 13) presented “persisted display preferences”; round 7 client (entry 14) accepted the app.
decisions.note: The final display-preference presentation conforms.
